artworks.title: Clotho
artworks.description: A plaster sculpture of Clotho, the Fate who spins the thread of life, imagined not as a maiden but as a gaunt old woman ensnared in the very threads she spins. Claudel's haunting inversion of the myth makes destiny itself appear entangled in its own web.

artworks.title: The Three Fates
artworks.description: An oil painting of the three Fates at their shared task: Clotho spinning the thread of life, Lachesis measuring it, and Atropos waiting with shears to cut it. The work is held in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Rome.

artworks.title: The Triumph of Death, or The Three Fates
artworks.description: A Brussels-school tapestry now in the Victoria and Albert Museum: Clotho, Lachesis and Atropos stand in triumph over the prostrate figure of Chastity, an allegory of Death drawn from Petrarch's Triumphs. Clotho, the spinner who begins each life, shares the foreground with her sisters' measure and shears.

artworks.title: The Fates Spinning Marie's Destiny
artworks.description: The opening canvas of Rubens' Marie de' Medici cycle in the Louvre: Clotho, Lachesis and Atropos spin the queen's thread beneath Jupiter and Juno. Clotho, the youngest Fate, draws the first filament — destiny cast as court allegory at the birth of a reign.

artworks.title: Peleus and Clotho (House of Theseus mosaic, Paphos)
artworks.description: Detail from the Achilles bath mosaic in the House of Theseus at Paphos Archaeological Park: King Peleus stands beside Clotho (Klotho) as the spinner of fate attends the infant hero's destiny. One of the clearest ancient labels of Clotho by name in surviving floor art.
